newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state to sell 20 pct of pharmaceutical firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state to sell 20 pct of pharmaceutical firm.

text.p: The Egyptian state's National Pharmaceuticals said on Monday it was offering investors at least 240,000 shares in Arab Drugs and Chemical Industries, or 20 percent of the equity.
The two-day flotation, part of the government's accelerating privatisation programme, will start on Tuesday with the National Bank of Egypt acting as agent, the parent company said.
Individual investors are offered 60,000 shares, the company added. This amount can be increased to meet demand.
The company is offering mutual funds and financial institutions 60,000 shares. The firm's employees are allocated the traditional portion of 10 percent, or 120,000 shares.
The shares are offered at a fixed price of 40 pounds a share.
Shareholders will be eligible for a dividend of at least 4.50 pounds for the financial year which ended on June 30, 1996, the company said.
The Egyptian state earlier this month sold off 40 percent of another pharmaceutical firm, Memphis Pharmaceutical and Chemical Industries, after the offer was met with huge demand.
Arab Drugs increased net profits for the 1995/96 financial year to 8.29 million pounds from 6.83 million a year earlier.
Net sales also rose to 94.13 million pounds from 85.22 million. They are expected to continue the uptrend to 108.15 million in the year 1996/97.
